threads.body: This sanitizes and reports a credential-bearing target, while the PR description explicitly says credential-bearing targets are omitted. The same behavior is asserted for both single- and multi-host inputs, so either reject any target containing user info here or update the stated requirement if sanitization is intended.

replies.body: Sanitization is intentional. The PR description now distinguishes removable credentials or user info from ambiguous or malformed credential-bearing inputs, which remain omitted.

threads.body: The new split changes `db.system.name` for pooled nested protocols, even though this PR is scoped to configured targets and promises legacy behavior remains unchanged. For example, `DRIVER=pool, PROTOCOL=clickhouse:http` previously resolved as `other_sql` because the full protocol was looked up, but now resolves as `clickhouse` in both semconv modes. Keep the old value for `systemName` and use the split values only for target/default-port handling.

replies.body: Restored the legacy `db.system.name` resolution. The split driver and protocol values are now used only for configured-target and default-port handling.

threads.body: Bracket syntax is stripped before the shared target builder validates the host, so malformed bracketed DNS names such as `[host1]:5432` are accepted and emitted as `host1` instead of causing the stable target to be omitted. Require a colon in the bracket contents before returning it; the existing builder validation will then verify that it is actually an IPv6 literal.

replies.body: Bracketed non-IPv6 hosts are now rejected in `R2dbcServerTarget`, with single-host and multi-host coverage added.

threads.body: This normalization depends only on the listener's immutable `factoryOptions`, but `DbExecution` is constructed for every query (`TraceProxyListener.java:34`). As written, every operation—including legacy-semconv operations that never read these fields—re-splits, validates, and allocates the target. Precompute the normalized address/port once when the listener is constructed and pass that immutable result into each execution.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: The current head already constructs one immutable `R2dbcConnectionInfo` from `factoryOptions` in the `TraceProxyListener` constructor. Each query passes that same snapshot to `DbExecution`, whose configured target getters only read the precomputed `DbServerTarget`. The production listener path no longer parses or normalizes the target per query.

Upsides: The current design removes the reported per-operation parsing and allocation while keeping all factory-derived connection attributes in one reusable snapshot.

Downsides: No material downside identified.
